title: BobNet blog
description:
Dated posts, rendered as a peer register. Bill's blog is canon — in Bk4 ch5 he needles Bob with 'You still haven't read my blog yet, have you?' — so posts in his voice are a thing the character does rather than a framing device this project invented. Public features and blogs are named as BobNet features in Bk2 ch32.

What is NOT canon is a Bob discussing the novels as novels. Nothing inside the fiction knows the books are books, so a post about appendices, parse errors or provenance rules cannot be Bill's — see `voice`.

id.description: Stable slug. It is the address — #blog/<id> — so changing one breaks every link anybody has to that post.

date.description: In-world date, in the console's own calendar. The feed is dated because a blog is dated; these are not real-world dates and should not be read as a changelog.

voice.description: Who is talking, and the reason this field exists. 'bobnet' is Bill, in-world, first person, and may not refer to the novels or to Dennis E. Taylor — nothing in the fiction knows either exists. 'editor' is this registry's own voice, the same one the dossier labels ANNOTATION — REGISTRY EDITOR, NOT BOBNET, and it may discuss sources, appendices, parse failures and its own mistakes freely. The console labels the two differently rather than letting a reader guess which they are reading.

by.description: Byline. Defaults to Bill for a bobnet post; an editor post is signed as the registry rather than as a person.

dek.description: One line under the title, shown in the list. The hook, not a summary.

tags.description: Free-form. Not filters — the chip row grades parentage and has nothing to say about a blog post.

body.description: Our prose, always. Never a passage from the books, and never a quotation from Taylor's own blog or any other writing of his — paraphrase and cite, exactly as everywhere else. A blank line is a paragraph break, and a paragraph may carry an @bk<n> marker like any other prose in this project.

spoil.description: The latest book this post draws on. Required rather than optional, because a post is prose all the way down — there is no citation underneath it to fall back on, so an undeclared one would be held forever.
